title: Pizza with beans and vegetables, thick crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with beans and vegetables on a thick crust combines nutritious beans, fresh vegetables, and a flavorful tomato sauce. The crust is dense yet tender, and the topping is rich in protein, fiber, and vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beans are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown by humans for over 7,000 years.
Thick‑crust pizzas require longer baking at a lower temperature compared to thin‑crust varieties.
The vegetables used (bell pepper, onion, tomatoes) are high in antioxidants that help combat free radicals.
Traditional Italian pizza is usually thin‑crusted, but many countries have developed thicker‑crust versions.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Beans provide a substantial amount of protein, essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber from beans and vegetables supports digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetable topping supplies vitamin C, vitamin A, and potassium, supporting immunity and skin health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Beans have a low glycemic index, helping to stabilize blood sugar levels.

items.title: Healthy fats in the crust
items.content: If the dough contains olive or vegetable oil, it adds monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to beans, experiencing anything from skin reactions to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: If the sauce or toppings are heavily salted, it can be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of beans can cause gas and bloating in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A thick crust makes the pizza more calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the pizza into serving pieces and enjoy it hot. You can add fresh leafy greens or a light yogurt drizzle for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore crust crispness.
